ground_truth_question: What is the primary purpose of BCG’s Global Data Protection Policy?
ground_truth_answer: The policy sets out the safeguards and procedures BCG uses to protect, handle, collect, process, retain, and store Personal Data that BCG owns, stores, maintains, or otherwise accesses. It also explains the broader framework of BCG global policies that support this purpose, ensuring our practices are consistent, controlled, and compliant across the firm.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: This Policy defines effective safeguards and procedures for protecting, handling, collecting, processing, retaining, and storing “Personal Data” that is owned, stored, maintained, or otherwise accessed by BCG. This Policy also articulates the framework of other BCG Global Policies designed to accomplish this purpose.

ground_truth_question: How does the policy define Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: Personal Data is any information about an identifiable individual. It covers data that directly identifies someone—such as a name, identification number, location data, or an online identifier—as well as combinations of attributes that describe aspects of a person’s identity, including physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: “Personal Data” is any information relating to an individual who can be identified by reference to a direct identifier (such as a name, an identification number, location data, or an online identifier) or by a combination of attributes describing the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural, or social identity of the individual.

ground_truth_question: Which data protection laws does BCG commit to comply with under this policy?
ground_truth_answer: BCG commits to comply with applicable data protection laws in the countries where it operates. The policy specifically references the EU General Data Protection Regulation, China’s Cybersecurity and Data Protection Law and the Personal Information Protection Law, and California’s Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act. These are examples and the commitment is not limited to these statutes.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: This Policy ensures that BCG: i. complies with data protection laws affecting the countries where BCG operates, including, but not limited to, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (“GDPR”), the China Cybersecurity and Data Protection Law and Personal Information Protection Law (“PIPL”), the California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (“CPRA”),

ground_truth_question: Who is covered by the Global Data Protection Policy?
ground_truth_answer: The policy applies worldwide to everyone associated with BCG, including employees, directors, Partners, officers, suppliers, agents, external contractors, and any other associated persons across BCG’s owned or controlled subsidiaries and affiliated entities, including Specialty Business Units.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: This Global Data Protection Policy (“policy”) applies worldwide to all employees, directors, Partners, officers, suppliers, agents, external contractors, and other persons associated with The Boston Consulting Group (“BCG”), its owned or controlled subsidiaries and affiliated entities (including Specialty Business Units (SBUs)).

ground_truth_question: Which external security frameworks does the policy align with?
ground_truth_answer: The policy is aligned with industry standards, specifically ISO/IEC 27001 control A.18.1.4 and the Information Security Forum’s Standard of Good Practice (SOGP), including IM1.2 Information Privacy and IM2 Information Protection.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Security Framework Alignment • ISO/IEC 27001: A.18.1.4 • ISF SOGP: IM1.2 Information Privacy, IM2 Information Protection

ground_truth_question: What does the principle of lawfulness, fairness, and transparency require at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: It requires that all Personal Data processed by BCG is handled in a lawful manner, fairly toward the individual, and with transparency so individuals understand how their data is used.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.1 Lawfulness, fairness, and transparency - Personal Data will be processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently.

ground_truth_question: How does BCG apply the purpose limitation principle?
ground_truth_answer: BCG collects Personal Data only for specified and legitimate purposes and processes it strictly to fulfill those purposes, avoiding use that is incompatible with the original intent.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.2 Purpose limitation - Personal Data will only be collected for specified and legitimate purposes and will only be processed to satisfy those purposes.

ground_truth_question: What is BCG’s approach to data minimization?
ground_truth_answer: BCG limits Personal Data to what is relevant and not excessive for the stated purpose, and when feasible and appropriate, deletes or anonymizes data based on business needs and associated risks.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.3 Data minimization – The Personal Data collected will be relevant and not excessive in relation to the purposes for which it is collected and processed. Personal Data will be deleted or rendered anonymous when feasible and appropriate based on BCG’s needs and the risks associated with its intended use.

ground_truth_question: What does the accuracy principle mean in practice?
ground_truth_answer: BCG keeps Personal Data up to date as needed and takes reasonable steps without unreasonable delay to correct or delete data it knows to be inaccurate or incomplete.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.4 Accuracy – Personal Data kept up to date as needed and, without unreasonable delay, BCG will take reasonable steps to correct or delete Personal Data which it becomes aware is inaccurate or incomplete.

ground_truth_question: How long does BCG keep Personal Data under the storage limitation principle?
ground_truth_answer: BCG keeps Personal Data only as long as necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, consistent with legal and business needs.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.5 Storage limitation – Personal Data will be kept for only if necessary for the purposes for which the Personal Data was collected.

ground_truth_question: What controls support integrity and confidentiality of Personal Data at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: Access or disclosure is restricted to individuals who need to know the information to support BCG’s legitimate business purposes or to fulfill applicable legal requirements.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.6 Integrity and confidentiality – Personal data will be accessed or disclosed only to those individuals who are reasonably required to know such information to accomplish BCG’s legitimate business purpose or to enable BCG to comply with applicable legal requirements.

ground_truth_question: How does BCG demonstrate accountability for Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: BCG implements appropriate technical and organizational measures to prevent unauthorized access, unlawful processing, and accidental loss, destruction, or damage.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.1.7 Accountability – Appropriate technical and organizational measures will be taken to prevent unauthorized access, unlawful processing and unauthorized or accidental loss, destruction, or damage to Personal Data.

ground_truth_question: Who is responsible for appropriate collection, storage, and handling of Personal Data at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: All BCG employees share responsibility. Managing Directors and Partners who lead case teams or functional teams must ensure Personal Data in their purview is handled in line with policies, laws, and regulations.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.2.1 All BCG employees have responsibility for ensuring Personal Data is collected, stored, and handled appropriately. Each Managing Director and Partner (MDP) leading case teams or functional teams (e.g., internal use scenarios) must ensure that Personal Data is handled and processed in line with applicable policies, laws, and regulations.

ground_truth_question: When BCG relies on consent, what are the core requirements before collecting Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: Consent must be obtained in advance, be specific and informed, and reflect an unambiguous agreement to process the individual’s Personal Data. If consent is part of a written form, it must be distinguishable, clear, and not bundled with other agreements or declarations.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.3.1.1 is obtained in advance of the collection of Personal Data. 1.3.1.2 is specific, informed and an unambiguous agreement to process an individual’s Personal Data. Where consent is part of a written form, consent will be distinguishable, clear, and not bundled with other written agreements or declarations.

ground_truth_question: If Personal Data will be used for more than one purpose, what must BCG communicate when seeking consent?
ground_truth_answer: BCG must adequately inform individuals about each purpose. It must also provide the identity and contact details of the data controller, the Data Protection Office’s contact, any third‑party recipients, any transfer to a third country if applicable, and the individual’s right to withdraw consent at any time.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Where Personal Data is processed for multiple purposes ... individuals will be adequately informed of each purpose. BCG will also inform individuals about: i. the identity and contact details of the data controller, ii. the contact details of the Data Protection Office iii. any third-party recipients of the personal data (if applicable), iv. the transfer of personal data to a third country (if applicable), and v. their right to withdraw consent at any time.

ground_truth_question: What conditions make consent valid at BCG, and what is expressly not allowed?
ground_truth_answer: Consent must be freely given and can be withdrawn at any time. It cannot be inferred from silence, inactivity, or pre‑ticked boxes, and non‑response cannot be treated as consent.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.3.1.3 is given freely. 1.3.1.4 is not inferred from non-response to a communication; inactivity, silence or pre‑ticked boxes are not permitted. 1.3.1.5 can be withdrawn at any time.

ground_truth_question: How does BCG handle consent for minors or Sensitive Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: When services involve a minor child, consent must be obtained from a parent or custodian. For Sensitive Personal Data—such as data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership; data concerning health, sex life, sexual orientation; criminal offenses, convictions, or related security measures; or genetic or biometric data uniquely identifying an individual—BCG requires explicit written consent.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.3.1.6 is obtained from a parent or custodian if/where BCG provides services to a minor child; and 1.3.1.7 is obtained by explicit written consent when processing Personal Data that reveals racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership or concerning health, sex life, sexual orientation, criminal offenses, convictions, or related security measures; genetic or biometric data or uniquely identifying the individual “Sensitive Personal Data”.

ground_truth_question: What records does BCG keep when relying on consent and how long are they retained?
ground_truth_answer: BCG maintains a retrievable consent log that serves as evidence for all types of consent and includes records of withdrawal requests. The consent log is kept for as long as BCG relies on consent as the lawful basis for processing.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.3.1.8 is recorded in retrievable records. The consent log will serve as evidence for all types of consent and include a record of all requests to withdraw consent. The consent log must be kept as long as BCG relies on consent as the lawful basis.

ground_truth_question: How does BCG approach cookie consent and do‑not‑track requests?
ground_truth_answer: BCG uses transparent mechanisms to obtain cookie consent where required and respects do‑not‑track requests from website visitors.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.3.1.9 is obtained with transparent mechanisms for required cookie consent from website visitors. BCG will respect do-not-track requests.

ground_truth_question: Beyond consent, what other lawful bases may BCG use to process Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: BCG may process Personal Data when necessary to perform a contract with the individual or to take pre‑contractual measures at the individual’s request; for important reasons of public interest; to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims; to protect someone’s vital interests when the individual cannot consent; and for legitimate interests pursued by BCG or a third party, except where those interests are overridden by the individual’s interests or fundamental rights and freedoms, particularly for a child.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.3.2 Other basis for processing ... 1.3.2.1 for the performance of a contract ... 1.3.2.2 for important reasons of public interest. 1.3.2.3 for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims. 1.3.2.4 to protect the vital interests ... 1.3.2.5 for the purposes of BCG’s legitimate interests ... except where such interests are overridden ... where the individual is a child.

ground_truth_question: When can Personal Data be transferred between BCG entities?
ground_truth_answer: Transfers occur only when there is a legitimate business need and the receiving entity provides appropriate security and certifies compliance with this policy and referenced policies. All such transfers comply with applicable laws, and BCG ensures intra‑group agreements include relevant standard contractual clauses as issued by authorities.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.4.1 Inter-company transfers will be done when there is a legitimate business need and only when the receiving entity provides appropriate security for the Personal Data and certifies to compliance with this Policy and the Policies referenced herein. ... BCG will ensure that intra-group agreements with the relevant standard contractual clauses, as issued by relevant authorities, under applicable data protection laws, have been entered by BCG’s operating entities globally.

ground_truth_question: Under what conditions does BCG disclose Personal Data to third parties?
ground_truth_answer: BCG prevents disclosure unless the third party has been authorized by BCG and/or the client and, where required by law, has signed a Data Processing Agreement. The policy highlights GDPR and Brazil’s LGPD as examples where a DPA may be required.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.5.1 BCG prevents disclosure of Personal Data to third parties, unless the third-party has been authorized by BCG and/or BCG’s client to receive Personal Data and has entered a Data Processing Agreement (“DPA”) where required by law (e.g., European GDPR, Brazilian LGPD).

ground_truth_question: What vetting and contractual terms apply when BCG engages a third‑party processor?
ground_truth_answer: Engagements must be vetted by Procurement, Information Security, and the Data Protection Office. Where required, a DPA must specify the subject matter and duration, the nature and purpose of processing, the types of personal data and categories of individuals, and the obligations and rights of both the third party and BCG.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.5.2 Where BCG engages a third-party processor that handles Personal Data, the engagement must be vetted by BCG Procurement, Information Security, and the Data Protection Office. Where required, a DPA must set out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of individuals and the obligations and rights of the third party and BCG.

ground_truth_question: Where can teams find approved supplier DPA templates and where should completed DPAs be stored?

exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.5.3 Approved supplier-DPA forms are available from BCG’s Global Procurement Team (ProcurementOps-DPAgreements@bcg.com) and completed DPAs must be sent to BCG’s Global Procurement Team to be stored in the global procurement contract database.

ground_truth_question: What are the requirements for contractors and temporary personnel who can access Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: Contractors and temporary personnel must use BCG-provided IT assets, sign a confidentiality agreement, complete mandatory privacy and security training, comply with BCG policies, and are subject to periodic performance review and monitoring by the Data Protection Office when they have access to Personal Data.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.5.3.1 Contractors and Temporary Personnel. Individuals working as contractors and temporary personnel who have access to Personal Data will: i. use company BCG-provided IT assets to perform their duties. ii. sign a confidentiality agreement. iii. participate in mandatory privacy and security training; and iv. comply with this policy and other applicable BCG policies. BCG’s Data Protection Office will periodically review and monitor the performance of its contractors and temporary personnel who have access to Personal Data.

ground_truth_question: When can BCG accept a transfer of Personal Data from a third party?
ground_truth_answer: BCG restricts transfers from third parties unless necessary for providing client products or services or to conduct BCG operations, and where required, a Data Processing Agreement is in place. The DPA must cover scope, duration, nature, purpose, data types, data subject categories, and the parties’ obligations and rights. An approved client DPA can be completed with Legal’s help via ClientView and should be sent to LegalTeam@bcg.com for the contract management system.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.5.4 BCG restricts the transfer of Personal Data from third parties unless such transfer is necessary for the provision of products and services to BCG’s client and/or to conduct BCG operations and BCG has entered a Data Processing Agreement (“DPA”) where required by law. 1.5.5 The DPA sets out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of individuals and the obligations and rights of the third party and BCG. 1.5.6 An approved client-DPA form is available and can be completed with the help of a Legal Team member (request via ClientView). Completed DPAs should be sent to LegalTeam@bcg.com to be included in teh contract management system.

ground_truth_question: How should Personal Data in paper or hard copy be removed from BCG or client premises?
ground_truth_answer: Any external transmission or removal of paper or hard-copy Personal Data must maintain the security of the information and prevent unauthorized disclosure.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.6.1 External transmission or removal of Personal Data in paper or hard-copy form from BCG or BCG client premises must be done in a manner to maintain the security of the data and prevent unauthorized disclosure.

ground_truth_question: What should I do before electronically transmitting Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: You should consult the Information Security Risk Management Team to select appropriate technical protections. Personal Data should not be shared informally and should not be sent by email, which is not a secure channel.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.6.2 Individuals who need to electronically transmit Personal Data should consult with BCG’s Information Security Risk Management Team (BCG ISRM Team) ... Personal data should not be shared informally. It should not be sent by email, as this form of communication is not secure.

ground_truth_question: How should paper records containing Personal Data be stored when unattended?
ground_truth_answer: They must be kept in a locked or otherwise secure desk, cabinet, office, or controlled area when unattended to prevent unauthorized access.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.7.1 Storage. Paper documents containing Personal Data must be stored in locked or otherwise secure desk, file cabinet, office, or controlled area when unattended.

ground_truth_question: What are the requirements for storing Personal Data electronically?
ground_truth_answer: Electronic Personal Data on laptops or portable devices must be protected with access controls and handled in accordance with BCG’s Global Information Security Policy. Personal Data should be stored only on designated drives, servers, and cloud services. Data must be backed up frequently and backups tested regularly, and systems containing Personal Data must be protected by approved security software and a firewall.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.7.1.1 Personal Data stored electronically on laptops or other portable devices must be protected via access controls and in accordance with BCG’s Global Information Security Policy. Personal Data should only be stored on designated drives, servers, and cloud services. 1.7.1.2 Data must be backed up frequently. Those backups should be tested regularly, in line with the company’s standard backup procedures. All servers and computers containing personal data must be protected by approved security software and a firewall.

ground_truth_question: Who is allowed to access or share files containing Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: Access, sharing, and disclosure are limited to people who require the information to achieve BCG’s legitimate business purposes or to help BCG meet legal requirements.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.7.2 Access, Sharing and Disclosure. Access to, sharing, and disclosure of records or files containing Personal Data is limited to persons who are reasonably required to know such data to accomplish the BCG’s legitimate business purposes or to enable BCG to comply with applicable legal requirements.

ground_truth_question: What physical precautions should individuals take with materials containing Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: Do not leave Personal Data in plain view or in unsecured or unattended locations. When leaving your office or work area, secure all files and records in line with this policy and physical security guidelines.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.7.2.1 Individuals must not leave materials containing Personal Data in plain view or in any unsecured or unattended locations. When leaving one’s office or work location, individuals must secure all files and other records containing Personal Data consistent with this Policy and other physical security guidelines.

ground_truth_question: What are the expectations for passwords and access termination for systems with Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: Personal Data should be protected by strong passwords that are changed regularly. Electronic access for former employees, former third‑party processors, and others who are no longer authorized must be terminated in accordance with BCG’s Account Management Standard, including when employees change roles.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.7.2.2 Personal Data should be protected by strong passwords that are changed regularly. BCG will terminate electronic access to records and files containing personal data by former employees, former third-party processors, and other individuals who are no longer authorized users with an active user account (e.g., employees moving into new roles). Electronic access will be terminated in accordance with BCG’s Account Management Standard.

ground_truth_question: How long does BCG retain Personal Data and how is retention reviewed?
ground_truth_answer: BCG retains Personal Data for the period reasonably required to achieve legitimate business purposes or to meet legal obligations. The firm periodically reviews records to ensure data is not kept longer than necessary and refers to the Global Data Retention Policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.8.1 Retention. BCG will maintain Personal Data for the length of time reasonably required for BCG to accomplish its legitimate business purposes, or such other period as necessary to comply with legal requirements ... BCG will periodically review records and files to ensure that it has not retained Personal Data for longer than there is a legitimate business reason or legal obligation to do so (see, BCG’s Global Data Retention Policy).

ground_truth_question: What must happen to Personal Data when a contract ends, a role changes, or upon request?
ground_truth_answer: BCG staff, contractors, and third‑party processors must return or destroy all records and files containing Personal Data upon contract or employment termination, resignation, role changes, or whenever BCG requests it.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.8.2 Return of Personal Data. BCG staff, contractors and third-party processors are required to return or destroy all records and files containing Personal Data upon contract or employment termination, resignation, role changes, or upon BCG’s request.

ground_truth_question: How should Personal Data be disposed of when no longer needed, and what if a legal hold applies?
ground_truth_answer: Electronic and paper records should be redacted, shredded, destroyed, or erased when appropriate. If destruction is prohibited by legal obligations, the data must be identified and preserved until lawful destruction is permitted, following the Global Data Retention Policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.8.3 Disposal of Personal Data. Where appropriate, electronic Personal Data or paper documents and other hard copies of records or files containing Personal Data, determined by BCG to be no longer needed, will be redacted, shredded, destroyed, or erased. If destruction of the data or records is prohibited by an existing legal obligation, the data or record will be identified and properly preserved until such time as it can be legally destroyed (see, BCG’s Global Data Retention Policy).

ground_truth_question: Where should individuals direct questions or concerns about their Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: They should contact BCG’s Data Protection Office at DataProtectionOffice@bcg.com, which coordinates processes to protect and address applicable rights.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Individuals having concerns should contact BCG’s Data Protection Office (DataProtectionOffice@bcg.com).

ground_truth_question: What rights do individuals have to access information BCG holds about them?
ground_truth_answer: Individuals can request access to Personal Data BCG holds about them and obtain information about the nature of the data and to whom it has been disclosed.

ground_truth_answer: Yes, in limited instances individuals may object to the processing of their Personal Data.

ground_truth_answer: BCG ensures individuals are aware their Personal Data is being processed and that they understand how it is used and how to exercise their rights. exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.10.1 BCG will ensure individuals are aware that their Personal Data is being processed, and that they understand how the Personal Data is being used and how to exercise their rights. ground_truth_question: What should I do if I become aware of a Personal Data breach at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: BCG complies with all required reporting and notification obligations in relevant jurisdictions. ground_truth_question: How should BCG respond to inquiries from a supervisory or data privacy authority?
ground_truth_answer: BCG will respond diligently to such requests, and all inquiries should be referred to the Data Protection Office at DataProtectionOffice@bcg.com.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.11.2 Obligations towards Supervising Authority/Local Data Privacy Authority. BCG will respond diligently to requests ... All requests should be referred to the Data Protection Office (DataProtectionOffice@bcg.com).

ground_truth_answer: BCG maintains records that include the controller’s contact details, the purposes of processing, categories of individuals and data, categories of recipients, details of cross‑border transfers, applicable retention periods, and a description of security measures applied to the processed data.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.12.1 BCG will keep records of its Personal Data processing activities which will include (i) contact details of the data controller; (ii) purposes of the processing; (iii) categories of individuals and personal data processed; (iv) categories of recipients ...; (v) information regarding cross-border data transfers; (vi) applicable data retention periods; and (vii) a description of the security measures implemented ...

ground_truth_question: What does data protection by design and by default mean at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: When BCG selects or develops new Personal Data processing tools, data protection is a key design consideration and is not sacrificed for other benefits. Applications are designed so individuals are protected by default from unnecessary processing, and the design must comply with the principles in this policy, including minimizing the amount of data collected, how it is processed, how long it is stored, and how accessible it is.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.13.1 When selecting or developing new Personal Data processing tools, BCG ensures, by design, that Personal Data is adequately protected ... BCG will design new applications such that any individuals who are the subject of personal data held by BCG are protected, by default, from increased risk due to unnecessary processing of Personal Data. Application design will comply with section 1.1 of this Policy (e.g., minimize the amount of Personal Data collected, the extent of their processing, the period of their storage, and accessibility).

ground_truth_question: How does BCG classify data to manage Personal Data throughout its lifecycle?
ground_truth_answer: BCG classifies data assets based on regulatory requirements, sensitivity, criticality, and value to the company. This classification enables adequate protection, effective management, easier access and use, and efficient retention and disposition. The approach is outlined in the Global Data Classification Policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.14.1 To enable adequate protection and effective management of Personal Data throughout its lifecycle, BCG classifies data assets based on regulatory requirements, sensitivity, criticality, and value to the company. Classification also allows for ease of access, use and management and the efficient retention and disposition of Personal Data (see, BCG’s Global Data Classification Policy).

ground_truth_question: What elements make up BCG’s approach to securing Personal Data?
ground_truth_answer: BCG maintains an Information Security Management System that includes an Information Security Risk Management Framework, related policies, and assigned roles and responsibilities. It covers access controls, physical and environmental security, and expectations for managing data assets as detailed in the Global Information Security Policy. The ISRM Team ensures required information security certifications are obtained and maintained.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.15.1 BCG has an Information Security Management System (“ISMS”) ... The ISMS also addresses access controls, physical and environmental security, and expectations for managing data assets (see, BCG’s Global Information Security Policy). The Information Security Risk Management Team (ISRM Team) will ensure all required information security certifications are obtained and maintained.

ground_truth_question: When does BCG conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) and what happens if high risk remains?
ground_truth_answer: The Data Protection Office, together with the Information Security Risk Management Team, conducts DPIAs for processing activities likely to result in high risk to individuals. Based on DPIA results, the ISRM Team applies appropriate security and privacy controls. If high risk remains in a proposed process, BCG consults the Regulatory Authority before processing to ensure controls sufficiently mitigate risks.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.16.1 ... will conduct Data Protection Impact Assessments (“DPIAs”) for processing activities considered likely to result in high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals ... ground_truth_question: When is a Data Transfer Impact Assessment (DTIA) required at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: DTIAs are conducted for processing activities that transfer Personal Data outside the European Economic Area and are subject to the GDPR or similar regimes. The ISRM Team applies appropriate controls based on the results, and if high risk persists, BCG consults with the Regulatory Authority prior to processing.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: 1.17.1 ... will conduct Data Transfer Impact Assessments (“DTIAs”) for processing activities resulting in the transfer of personal data to outside the European Economic Area (EEA) and subject of the European GDPR or other jurisdictions where similar requirements exist. Based on the results of the DTIAs ... If the DTIA reveals high risk ... BCG will consult with the Regulatory Authority prior to processing ...

ground_truth_question: Who must complete privacy and security awareness training at BCG?
ground_truth_answer: All employees, contractors, MDPs, and temporary personnel who access Personal Data must complete training aligned to their data protection responsibilities.
